summary: American-born inventor Hiram Maxim built the first practical machine gun in the 1880s and sold it to every power he could, enabling British colonial massacres in Africa and the slaughter of the First World War.

evidence.note: uncle's workshop in Massachusetts; curling iron patent 1866
chief engineer at US Electric Lighting, rivalry with William Sawyer
1881 Paris Exposition prompts work on the machine gun
Zaharoff sabotages Maxim's sales, then the companies merge
Battle of Shangani in modern Zimbabwe, Matabele massacred by Maxim guns
Woodville illustrations erase the machine gun from British war imagery
sells to both sides in 1905; naturalised British in 1900
death in 1916 during the Somme; WWI machine-gun toll

notes: Packet footnotes cite Gerald Bull, who is the part two subject announced at the end and not covered here. Transcript says the Emin Pasha relief faced Mahdists and that the Matabele leader killed himself at Shangani; both differ from standard histories, so the Sudan/Equatoria setting and suicide warning were left out. Masculinity-and-the-rifle segment has no close theme.
